title: 2026 Michigan gubernatorial election
description: Michigan's 2026 gubernatorial election will choose the state's next governor after term-limited Democrat Gretchen Whitmer leaves office. The open seat is one of five Democratic-held governorships up for election in a state that Donald Trump won in the 2024 presidential election, heightening the stakes in this battleground state. The Democratic primary features Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson and Genesee County Sheriff Chris Swanson, while the Republican field includes U.S. Representative John James, state Senate Republican Leader Aric Nesbitt, former Attorney General Mike Cox, and businessman Perry Johnson. Former Detroit Mayor Mike Duggan launched an independent bid but withdrew in May 2026, leaving the general election as a contest between the Democratic and Republican nominees in a state where both parties see a path to victory.

candidates.name: Jocelyn Benson
candidates.summary: Jocelyn Benson is Michigan’s secretary of state and a Democratic candidate for governor in 2026. Her campaign has centered on affordability, including housing, healthcare, childcare, energy costs, and government reform, while also emphasizing election administration and voter access.

Healthcare.stance: Healthcare remains a core affordability and access issue for Michigan. Benson's plan centers on reducing costs through system reform, including creating an independent Prescription Drug Affordability Board to review pricing and approve price changes, expanding low- and no-cost preventive care, implementing cost transparency to end surprise medical bills, and transforming the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services to be more responsive and debt-relief oriented; it also includes a $5,000 caregiver tax credit and continued focus on Black maternal health and access to care in high-need communities.

candidates.name: Chris Swanson
candidates.summary: Genesee County Sheriff Chris Swanson is a Democratic candidate for Michigan governor in 2026. A career law enforcement officer with over 30 years at the Genesee County Sheriff's Office, he was appointed sheriff in 2019 and elected in 2020 and 2024. Swanson gained national attention in May 2020 for removing his riot gear and marching with protesters in Flint after George Floyd's murder, and his campaign emphasizes criminal-justice reform, public education investment, and local control over development.

Tech & AI.stance: Swanson supports strong local control and public input for data-center siting, preferring a three-color zoning framework (yellow for infrastructure-ready areas, green for open with safeguards, red for limited or no deployment) to guide where centers can locate. He also advocates requiring data centers to invest in local generation or otherwise protect ratepayers, and opposes subsidies or top-down mandates.

Economy.stance: Swanson's Build in Michigan plan aims to grow the economy with good-paying union jobs, protect prevailing wage and worker safety, and foster entrepreneurship through an Office of Innovation; it also prioritizes Career and Technical Education in middle and high school to prepare students for skilled trades, aims to raise literacy, and seeks to lower energy costs by increasing energy production and ensuring rate increases by utilities occur only with better service.

candidates.voting_summary: Incumbent Michigan State Senator (District 20) since 2019, previously served in the State House (2011–2016). As Senate Minority Leader, he has been a leading Republican voice opposing Democratic budgets, which he has described as raising taxes and continuing reckless spending. His sponsored legislation includes bills on election administration, environmental regulation, and daylight saving time. Michigan League of Conservation Voters tracks his environmental votes.
candidates.donor_summary: Raised approximately $2.7 million through October 2025, with $2.2 million cash on hand at year-end 2025. Top individual max donors include Carol and David Van Andel (Amway/Van Andel Institute), Sidney Jansma (Wolverine Gas and Oil), Mark Fazakerley (Eagle Alloy), Ron Boji (Boji Group), and Chris Yatooma. Nearly $1 in every $5 he has raised came through a GOP network described as a conduit for large out-of-state donations.

candidates.summary: Anthony Hudson is a Genesee County truck driver and political newcomer running for Michigan governor under the Libertarian Party. Born in Texas and a Michigan resident since 2012, he previously sought the Republican nomination but switched parties in February 2026. His platform centers on eliminating property and state income taxes, returning power to local communities, and reducing the size of state government.

Economy.stance: Eliminate property taxes and the state income tax and replace them with a county-level tax system that funds local services; advocate for reducing the gas tax and prioritizing small-business growth to drive economic development.

forecast.rationale: This remains an open-seat battleground race with only very limited polling evidence. The only 2026 poll cited in the provided data is an April IPPSR/MSU survey describing Jocelyn Benson as having only a slight lead and explicitly saying there was no clear frontrunner; no numeric candidate percentages are available, so the polling cannot support more than a minimal edge. Democrats have some candidate-strength advantages in the current field, especially Benson's statewide office profile and stronger Democratic fundraising, while Republicans also have multiple credible and well-funded contenders in a state Donald Trump carried in 2024. Because the nomination picture is still unsettled and the available polling is sparse and non-numeric, the race is best treated as a tossup with a very slight Democratic edge rather than a clearly favored party.
